text:
elaine: rolling out NF4/FP4 patch to canary yesterday, seeing steady throughput drop (~25%) and periodic memory spikes on pool-3. Can anyone confirm if this matches what you saw?

jon: seeing same. p95 latency up, token/sec down. suspect kernel selection fell back to elementwise FP path for attention.

maria: quick note — calibration step changed per-shard scales, might've increased kv cache footprint for long contexts. not 100% sure.

shiv: pinging perf-bot for profiling traces and whether continuous batching behavior changed.

perf-bot: attached CPU/GPU flame summary for the window 1763456600-1763456800:
```
GPU0: 41% time in nf4_attention_kernel_small_seq, 28% time in fp4_attention_fallback, 18% memory copies, 13% other
CPU: batching_worker blocked on copy_to_device, avg wait 12ms
Total tokens/sec: 38k (baseline 52k)
Memory spike: GPU0 used 13.2GB -> 18.7GB at drop point
```

elaine: that fp4_attention_fallback line looks bad — kernel selection may be incorrectly classifying batch shapes and choosing slower code path. any recent changes to selector heuristics?

jon: I pushed a heuristic tweak yesterday to prefer FP4 for per-token > 512, but NF4 kernels actually beat FP4 for our typical seq=256 microbatches. mis-tuned threshold.

maria: also saw calibration now inserts a per-layer weight scale table on host which we mmap at startup. that increased pinned memory usage and triggered a bigger copy during evictions (KV cache churn).

shiv: reproduce locally with stress tool:
```bash
./stress_infer --model redwood-nf4-1b --batch-shapes "[1,256],[4,128],[2,512]" --kv-ttl 600 --workload 60m
```
Result: same drop. Heap growth aligns with cache writes during rollouts.

elaine: good repro. what's the quickest mitigation? can we force the old kernel selection until we fix heuristics?

jon: yes — runtime flag exists: kernel_selector.force_prefer_nf4=true. patching canary now. will also add safety guard: if observed tokens/sec < baseline*0.85 then auto-roll back.

maria: deploying patch to reduce mmaped scale table size — change: use uint16 quant params instead of float32. trades tiny accuracy for memory.

infra-bot: deploy started by jon to canary cluster pool-3 at 1763456842.

perf-bot: quick follow after 2m: throughput recovered to ~50k tokens/sec, memory stable ~13.5GB. p95 latency back to baseline.

elaine: awesome, thanks. action items: (1) jon to revert selector thresholds and add test vectors for seq distributions, (2) maria to run quant param quantization follow-up with eval set to ensure no regression, (3) shiv to add KV cache eviction tracepoints around mmap and copy.

jon: will open PR with revert + unit tests. tagging @maria for perf regression eval.

maria: will run eval suite and share quality vs speed delta. initial estimate: <0.3% LL change for uint16 quant params.

elaine: update thread with PR links and postmortem once stable. :thumbsup:

jon: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/3421 (force selector revert + auto-rollback)

maria: eval results gist: https://gist.github.com/maria/4bit-calib-eval (summary: speed +18%, mean LL diff 0.002)

elaine: closing canary after monitoring window. will schedule deeper kernel selector audit next week.

perf-bot: monitoring will run for 24h and alert on >10% regresison from baseline.

elaine: thanks all. if anyone notices other noisy nodes, drop logs here.
